tabs.openServerHint: Pick one from the sidebar or search for it.

terminal.exited: Process exited with code {{code}}. Press Enter to restart.
terminal.exitedUnknown: Process exited. Press Enter to restart.

key.selectHint: Hold your finger on the text to select it.

monitor.unsupported: Resource monitoring is only available on Linux servers

settings.title: Settings
settings.highlightHint: Colours IP addresses, errors, warnings, dates and URLs in plain command output (tcpdump, logs…). Programs that use their own colours are left untouched.
settings.screenReader: Screen reader mode in the terminal
settings.screenReaderHint: For VoiceOver and other screen readers: terminal output is read as it arrives.
settings.appLockHint: Asks for Face ID, Touch ID or the device password when the app opens and when you come back after a minute.

ssh.failed:
Connection failed: {{error}}
Press Enter to reconnect.
ssh.closed: Connection closed. Press Enter to reconnect.

host.name: Name
host.nameHint: How it appears in the list.
host.passwordHint: Stored in your system keychain. Leave empty to be asked each time.
host.passphraseHint: Only if the key is encrypted. Stored in your system keychain.
host.agentHint: Uses the keys loaded in your SSH agent (ssh-agent, 1Password, Pageant…). Nothing is stored in Hostealo Terminal.
host.deleteBody: {{name}} and its saved password will be removed from this computer. Open sessions stay connected.
host.colorHint: Tints the terminal for this host, e.g. red for production.
host.folderHint: Use / for subfolders, e.g. Clients/Acme. You can also drag hosts onto folders.
host.ftpInsecure: Plain FTP sends your password unencrypted. Use FTPS if the server supports it.
host.ftpsHint: FTP over TLS (AUTH TLS), the encrypted FTP offered by Plesk, cPanel and most hosting panels.
host.rdpHint: Windows Remote Desktop (also xrdp). Use DOMAIN\user for domain accounts. On a Mac, ⌘ works as Ctrl in the session.
host.sharedFolderHint: Appears on the remote computer as the “Hostealo” drive (This PC), to copy files both ways. Leave empty to share nothing.
host.commandsHostHint: A saved SSH host for this same server: the AI agent runs its commands there and reads their output, which is faster and more reliable than clicking. Windows Server 2019 and later include OpenSSH; to turn it on, run this in an administrator PowerShell on the server:

hostKey.unknownBody: This is the first time you connect to {{host}}. Check that the fingerprint matches the server before trusting it.
hostKey.changedBody: {{host}} is presenting a different key than the one on record. This could mean someone is intercepting the connection, or the server was reinstalled. Don't continue unless you know why it changed.

auth.retry: That didn't work. Please try again.

knownHosts.title: Known hosts
knownHosts.description: Fingerprints of the servers you trust. Reinstalled a server with the same IP? Search for it and forget its old key, here and in ~/.ssh/known_hosts.
knownHosts.search: Search by host or IP (e.g. 203.0.113.10 or host:2222)
knownHosts.hashedHint: OpenSSH stored this host name hashed. Search for its exact host or IP to find it.
knownHosts.backupNote: Before ~/.ssh/known_hosts is changed, a copy is saved as ~/.ssh/known_hosts.old.
knownHosts.confirmForget: All keys recorded for {{target}} will be deleted. The next connection will ask you to trust the server again.
knownHosts.confirmRemove_one: The selected key will be deleted. The next connection will ask you to trust the server again.
knownHosts.confirmRemove_other: The {{count}} selected keys will be deleted. The next connections will ask you to trust the servers again.

keys.title: SSH keys
keys.description: Key pairs in your ~/.ssh folder. Copy a public key to a server's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys to log in without a password.
keys.emptyHint: Generate one to log in to your servers without passwords.
keys.usageHint: To use a key, choose “Private key” when editing a host and select its file.
keys.deleteBody: {{path}} and its .pub file will be deleted. This cannot be undone, and servers that only accept this key will stop letting you in.
keys.createdBody: Saved as {{path}}. This is its public key:
keys.ed25519Hint: Recommended: small, fast and secure. Supported by any current server.
keys.ecdsaHint: NIST P-256 curve. Use it if a system requires ECDSA.
keys.rsaHint: For old servers that do not support Ed25519. Takes a few seconds to generate.
keys.name: File name
keys.passphraseHint: Protects the key if someone copies the file.

sftp.name: Name
sftp.dropHint: Drop files here to upload them
sftp.deleteFolder: The folder {{name}} and everything in it will be deleted from the server.
sftp.deleteFile: {{name}} will be deleted from the server.
sftp.deleteMany_one: {{count}} item will be deleted from the server, including folder contents.
sftp.deleteMany_other: {{count}} items will be deleted from the server, including folder contents.

folders.name: Folder name
folders.deleteBody: The empty folder {{name}} will be deleted.
folders.deleteBodyHosts_one: The folder {{name}} will be deleted. Its {{count}} host moves up one level; no host is deleted.
folders.deleteBodyHosts_other: The folder {{name}} will be deleted. Its {{count}} hosts move up one level; no host is deleted.

certificate.title: Unverified certificate
certificate.body: The certificate of {{host}} could not be verified. On shared hosting this is common: the certificate is often issued for the provider's server name, or self-signed. Trust it only if the fingerprint is the one you expect.
certificate.changedBody: {{host}} is presenting a different certificate than the one you trusted. It may have been renewed, or someone may be intercepting the connection.

rdp.connectFailed: Could not connect to the remote desktop
rdp.ctrlAltDel: Send Ctrl+Alt+Del to the remote computer

clipboard.remoteFiles_one: {{count}} file copied on the remote computer
clipboard.remoteFiles_other: {{count}} files copied on the remote computer
clipboard.chooseFolder: Choose where to save the copied files
clipboard.saving: Saving files from the remote computer…

rdp.noSharedFolder: No folder is shared with this server
rdp.sharedFolderHeading: Shows in Windows as the “Hostealo” drive (This PC)
rdp.sharedFolderExplain: Share a folder from this computer and it shows in Windows as the “Hostealo” drive, to move files both ways.
rdp.audioPlaying: Sound: arriving from the server and playing here
rdp.audioFailed: Sound: arriving but it cannot be played here ({{error}})
rdp.audioWaiting: Sound: the server has sent none yet (play something in Windows; if it stays like this, check that the “Windows Audio” service is running)

ai.title: AI assistant
ai.connectBody: Use your Claude subscription through Claude Code, a Claude or OpenAI API key, or a local model with Ollama. Questions go straight to your provider.
ai.intro: Ask anything about this session. Commands it suggests don't run until you click “Run”.

suggestions.failed: Why did the last command fail?
suggestions.disk: What is taking up the most disk space?
suggestions.howto: How do I check which services are listening on a Linux server?
suggestions.firewall: Open port 443 in the firewall without cutting off my SSH

ai.includeOutputHint: Sends the terminal's latest lines with your question
ai.noOutputHint: This tab is not a terminal
ai.includeScreenHint: Sends a screenshot of the remote desktop with your question
ai.refusedBody: It declined this request. Rephrase the question or try another model.
ai.insertHint: Types the command in the terminal without running it
ai.runHint: Types the command in the terminal and presses Enter
ai.confirmRunBody: It may delete data, cut the connection or restart the machine. Make sure it is what you want.

form.title: AI assistant

about.claudeCode: Uses your Claude subscription (Pro or Max) through Claude Code installed on this computer. No API key: it counts towards your plan's limits.
about.anthropic: Claude, by Anthropic. Create a key at console.anthropic.com.
about.openai: OpenAI models. Create a key at platform.openai.com.
about.ollama: Models running on your computer with Ollama: nothing leaves your machine.
about.compatible: Any server with the OpenAI API: LM Studio, vLLM, OpenRouter…

form.apiKeyHint: Kept in the system keychain, never in a file.
form.apiKeyOptional: Only if your server asks for one. Kept in the system keychain.
form.baseUrlHint: Leave it empty to use the provider's.
form.baseUrlRequiredHint: The API address, usually ending in /v1.
form.modelHint: Type the name or use the button to see the available ones.
form.modelsFound_one: {{count}} model available: pick it from the list or type another.
form.modelsFound_other: {{count}} models available: pick one from the list or type another.
form.modelsFailed: Could not get the model list: {{error}}
form.effortHint: How much Claude reasons before answering: more effort gives more careful replies, slower and costlier.
form.privacy: Each question sends the session details (server, system) and, if ticked, the terminal's latest lines to your provider. Make sure they hold no secrets.
form.cliPathHint: Leave it empty to find it automatically.
form.cliMissing: Claude Code is not on this computer. Install it and run `claude` once to sign in, or enter its path.
form.cliModelPlaceholder: opus, sonnet, haiku… (empty: Claude Code's own)

agent.label: Agent
agent.hint: The AI runs the commands itself, asking for your permission for each one
agent.intro: Agent mode: give it a task (for example “install nginx and check it answers”) and the AI runs the steps on this server. Every command asks for your permission first.
agent.autoApprove: Approve commands that are not dangerous automatically
agent.limit: Step limit: tell it to go on if you want to continue
agent.notConnected: The SSH session is not connected

rdp.intro: Ask about what is on the remote desktop: with “{{screen}}” ticked, the AI sees a screenshot with your question.
rdp.agentIntro: Agent mode: give it a task and the AI does it on this server, with commands over SSH and/or the mouse and keyboard. Every step asks for your permission first.
rdp.noReach: To act on this server, let the AI use the mouse and keyboard, or link an SSH host for commands in the host settings.
rdp.desktopControl: Let the AI use the mouse and keyboard
rdp.desktopControlHint: It sees a screenshot after each step. Slower than commands: best for things only the graphical interface can do.

suggestions.error: Explain the error on the screen and how to fix it
suggestions.services: Which Windows services failed to start?

desktop.invalid: The AI sent an action that is not valid; it was told to try again.

import.title: Import servers
import.intro: Bring your connections over from other apps, folders included. You can review the list before importing.
import.passwordsNote: Encrypted passwords (MobaXterm, Royal, PuTTY) are not imported: the app asks for them when connecting and can keep them in the keychain. FileZilla passwords without a master password are imported, straight into the keychain.
import.empty: No connection that can be imported was found in this file.
import.intoHint: The other app's folders are created inside it. Leave it empty to import them at the top level.

hostealo.title: Hostealo account
hostealo.intro: Connect your account and your VPS and dedicated servers show up in the sidebar on their own, always with their current IP. From each VPS's menu you can start, stop or restart it.
hostealo.step1: In the client area, go to Account → API Keys and create a key. Read permission is enough; to start and stop VPS, read and write.
hostealo.step2: Paste it here. It is kept in the system keychain.
hostealo.apiKeyHint: You can revoke it from the panel at any time.
hostealo.connectedBody: Your VPS and dedicated servers appear in the Hostealo/VPS and Hostealo/Dedicados folders and stay up to date on their own: when the app starts and every few minutes. If you rename or move one, that is kept; if you delete it, it does not come back.
hostealo.syncResult: {{total}} servers in your account: {{added}} added and {{updated}} with an updated IP.
hostealo.pending_one: {{count}} is being set up and will appear once it has an IP.
hostealo.pending_other: {{count}} are being set up and will appear once they have an IP.
hostealo.importHint: Adds your VPS and dedicated servers automatically

power.startBody: The start order is sent to the VPS through the Hostealo panel.
power.restartBody: The VPS will restart: open connections drop for a few seconds.
power.stopBody: The VPS will shut down and stay off until you start it again.

hostealo.resetPasswordBody: The panel does not store the current password, so it cannot be read: a new one is set on the VPS and saved in the system keychain so you are not asked again. The old password stops working. It needs an API key with write permission.

files.localHint: Drag to the server to upload · double-click uploads the file
files.remoteHint: Drag to the left to download · double-click downloads the file
files.localDeleteNote: It is deleted from this computer, without going to the bin.
files.windowsSshHint: A Windows server's files go over its SSH server, which is usually off. To turn it on, in PowerShell as administrator: Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Server~~~~0.0.1.0; Start-Service sshd; Set-Service sshd -StartupType Automatic. Meanwhile, you can move files with the remote desktop's shared folder.
files.localHintIos: Also in Files › On My iPhone › Hostealo Terminal
files.localHintIpad: Also in Files › On My iPad › Hostealo Terminal
files.phoneHint: Tap a folder to open it · hold to select

sync.title: Sync devices
sync.intro: Open this window on the other device too. On the same network (Wi-Fi or cable) they find each other; if not, use the QR code. Nothing goes through the internet.
sync.visibleHint: only while this window is open
sync.none: Looking… open “Sync devices” on the other device.
sync.manual: Not listed? Paste the link or the address
sync.compare: Check that “{{name}}” shows the same code:
sync.why: If the codes match, nobody got in between.
sync.includeSecretsHint: They travel encrypted from one device to the other and go into its keychain. Unticked, only servers and folders are synced.
sync.waitingOther: Waiting for the other device to confirm…
sync.rejected: Sync cancelled: the codes did not match.
sync.qrHint: Scan it with the iPhone or iPad camera: the app opens and they connect with no codes to compare. On another computer, copy the link and paste it there under “Not listed?”.
sync.paired: Paired with “{{name}}” through the QR code: the connection is verified.

backup.intro: To move to a new computer, or when the devices share no network: save everything to a file encrypted with a passphrase and open it on the other one. If it already has servers, they are combined.
backup.passphraseHint_one: At least {{count}} character. Without it the backup cannot be opened: there is no way to recover it.
backup.passphraseHint_other: At least {{count}} characters. Without it the backup cannot be opened: there is no way to recover it.
backup.includeSecretsHint: They go inside the encrypted file. Unticked, only servers and folders are saved.
backup.importHint: The one you set when exporting.
backup.keepPassphrase: Keep the passphrase somewhere safe: without it the backup cannot be opened.

sync.scanSteps: On the computer, open Hostealo Terminal and “Sync devices”. Then open the Camera app, point it at the QR code and tap “Open in Hostealo Terminal”.
sync.phoneLink: Rather start from the computer? Copy this device's link and paste it there under “Not listed?”.
sync.networkHint: Both devices must be able to reach each other on the network: if one is on a VPN or another Wi-Fi, they won't connect. Use “Encrypted backup” then.
sync.manualPhone: Paste the link or the address
sync.introPhone: Move your servers between the computer and this device directly over your network: nothing goes through the internet.

snippets.title: Quick commands
snippets.noTerminal: Open a terminal to use them.
snippets.emptyHint: Save the commands you type again and again and run them on any server without retyping. They sync with your other devices.
snippets.insertHint: Type it into the terminal without running it
snippets.dangerous: Can delete data or stop the service
snippets.keys: Click: type it · ▶ or Enter: run it · ⇧Enter: only type it
snippets.deleteBody: “{{name}}” will also be deleted on your other devices when they sync.
snippets.dangerBody: It can delete data, cut the connection or shut the server down.
snippets.name: Name
snippets.nameHint: To find it; left empty, the command is used.
snippets.commandHint: With several lines, they run one after the other. ⌘Enter to save.
snippets.dangerNote: This command can be dangerous: it asks for confirmation before running.

status.title: Status
status.description: The servers you are connected to, live, and the alerts about them. Checked over the session's own connection: nothing is installed on the server.
status.emptyTitle: You are not connected to any server
status.emptyHint: Open an SSH session to see its CPU, memory, disk and network here, with alerts when something goes wrong.
status.alertsOff: Alerts are turned off in Settings.

kind.memory: Memory at {{value}} % for over a minute
kind.cpu: CPU at {{value}} % for over two minutes

settingsAlerts.title: Alerts
settingsAlerts.enabled: Alert me about problems on connected servers
settingsAlerts.notify: Also as a system notification when the app is in the background

palette.title: Search
palette.placeholder: Find a server, a tab, a command or an action…
palette.keys: ↑↓ move · Enter open · {{modifier}}+Enter new session · Esc close

docker.title: Docker · {{name}}
docker.empty: There are no containers on this server.
docker.name: Container
docker.removeBody: The container is stopped and deleted. Its volumes are kept; whatever it stored inside without a volume is lost.

missing.title: Docker is not installed on this server
missing.hint: Install it with the official script (curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh) or from your system's packages.

permission.title: Your user is not allowed to use Docker
permission.hint: Add it to the docker group (sudo usermod -aG docker $USER and reconnect) or connect as root.

daemon.title: Docker does not answer
daemon.hint: The service may be stopped: try systemctl start docker.

vms.title: Virtual machines · {{name}}
vms.empty: There are no virtual machines on this server.
vms.name: Machine
vms.forceOffBody: Like pulling the plug: it stops at once, without shutting the system down. Unsaved work may be lost. Use “Shut down” if it responds.
vms.libvirtNote: Managed directly with virsh. If this server is a SolusVM node, the panel sees the changes at its next sync.

none.title: No Proxmox or KVM here
none.hint: This view is for Proxmox VE nodes and KVM servers with libvirt (such as SolusVM 2 nodes). Connect to one of them.

permission.title: Your user cannot manage the machines
permission.hint: Connect as root, or allow passwordless sudo for pvesh or virsh.

daemon.title: The virtualization service does not answer
daemon.hint: libvirt or Proxmox is not running on this server: try systemctl start libvirtd (or pve-cluster on Proxmox).

lock.title: Hostealo Terminal is locked
lock.hint: Use Face ID, Touch ID or the device password to get in.
